dod_intent_evidence: Three Air Force SBIR Phase II awards in 2023 (Mode 5 TLS for Agile Combat Employment, roll-on/roll-off ATC, autonomous voice-over-localizer) plus a Jan-2024 AFWERX Phase 2 announcement on their own site — SBIR record and news sections.
score_evidence: "Designed for use at temporary or remote airfields, often in austere environments" → deployment_awareness_absence scored low; language is operational, not lab
"To pilots, TLS is indistinguishable from a standard ILS—requiring no new avionics or training" → operator_absence scored low; training burden explicitly engineered away
Open roles include "Field Service Technician" and "Configuration Management Manager" → hiring_profile_skew scored low; field and sustainment roles are being hired
Three concurrent 2023 Phase II periods of performance (SBIR record) → stage_pressure moderate; three transition clocks running at once on one mature small business

blind_spots.blind_spot: Three simultaneous Phase II transition clocks with no visible transition partner or program-of-record path named anywhere in their language
blind_spots.operator_reality: ACE deployments need the eTLS to move from SBIR demo to a funded sustainment and fielding pipeline; when the 2023 periods of performance lapse, all three efforts hit the valley at once
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: A 30-year commercial ILS vendor is fluent in civil aviation certification, not DoD transition mechanics — SBIR is a new motion for them (first Phase IIs 2023)
blind_spots.evidence_quote: ANPC announces it has been selected by AFWERX for a SBIR Phase 2 contract

blind_spots.blind_spot: No ATO/RMF or cybersecurity accreditation language anywhere despite selling a system that must plug into USAF air traffic control and Mode 5 IFF infrastructure
blind_spots.operator_reality: A transportable ATC system at a contingency airfield connects to government networks and crypto (Mode 5); without an accreditation story the box sits in a conex while the ATO paperwork ages
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their civil-aviation heritage is FAA/ICAO certification — a different regulatory language than RMF/STIGs, and their site never bridges the two
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Fully compliant with ICAO and FAA Category I ILS requirements

blind_spots.blind_spot: Sustainment at austere sites is asserted ("setup to full operational capacity in a manner of hours") but the who-fixes-it chain is silent — spares, battery logistics, and the airman who maintains eTLS after the ANPC tech goes home
blind_spots.operator_reality: An expeditionary ILS that fails at a bare base with no ANPC Field Service Technician in theater grounds the approach capability the whole ACE concept depends on
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Commercial airport customers buy installation plus service contracts; ACE dispersal assumes organic military maintenance they have not publicly addressed
blind_spots.evidence_quote: transported by land, air and sea and setup to full operational capacity in a manner of hours

opener_hook: ANPC is running three Air Force Phase II clocks from 2023 at once — Mode 5 TLS, roll-on/roll-off ATC, and the autonomous voice-over-localizer all reach the same transition wall together.
what_they_do: Transponder-based instrument landing and airfield surveillance systems for terrain-challenged and austere airfields, now being adapted for USAF Agile Combat Employment.
